issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Add Food modal (CustomMealModal) never resets its Ingredients-tab state on close — a stale ingredient selection or half-filled "Add new" custom-macros form reappears on reopen and can be logged by accident.

Route: /nutrition (Add Food bottom sheet, Ingredients tab).

Expected: closing the modal returns it to a fresh state (Quick Log tab, empty ingredient search, no selected ingredient, empty new-ingredient form) — the same way the Quick-Log macro fields already reset on close (QA i-20260711-d0ca).

Actual: the reset-on-close effect (src/components/nutrition/CustomMealModal.tsx:131-137) clears ONLY quickMacros / showQuickMacros / estimateConfidence. It never clears activeTab, ingredientQuery, selectedIngredient, ingServings, ingIsSaved, isAddingNew, customMacros, or photoMacros. The modal is mounted unconditionally by Nutrition.tsx (only its inner DOM is gated on isOpen — see mic-cleanup note, CustomMealModal.tsx:118-127), so this state survives every open/close. Parent closeCustomMealModal (src/pages/Nutrition.tsx:368-371) resets only customMealText, not the modal internal ingredient state.

Repro:
1. Nutrition -> tap "+ Log Food" to open Add Food.
2. Tap the "Ingredients" tab -> tap "Add new ingredient with custom macros".
3. Type name "Dark chocolate", Calories 500, Protein 5.
4. Close the modal with the X (do NOT log).
5. Reopen Add Food (+ Log Food).
Expected: fresh modal on Quick Log with an empty ingredient form.
Actual: modal reopens on the Ingredients tab with the "Add new" form still showing Dark chocolate / 500 / 5 and an active "Add to Today" button — one tap logs a meal the user never meant to. Same leak for a previously selected search result plus its servings count.

Fix: extend the !isOpen reset effect (or the parent close handler) to also clear ingredient-tab state: setActiveTab("quick"), setIngredientQuery(""), setSelectedIngredient(null), setIngServings(1), setIngIsSaved(false), setIsAddingNew(false), setCustomMacros(empty), setPhotoMacros(null) — mirroring the d0ca quick-log reset.

Aside (not filed separately): updateIngredientMutation (CustomMealModal.tsx:159-164) is dead code — defined but never invoked.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Partner invites: Accept and Decline fail silently — zero feedback on any error.

Route: /partners/invites (src/pages/PartnerInvites.tsx).

What is wrong: acceptMutation (lines 37-52) and declineMutation (lines 54-60) have ONLY onSuccess/onSettled — NO onError handler. The app QueryClient (src/App.tsx:163-173) sets defaultOptions.queries only; there is NO mutations MutationCache/global onError. So when either POST rejects, react-query swallows it: onSettled clears busyId (button re-enables), but there is no toast, no navigation, and the mutation does NOT refetch, so the invite row stays on screen unchanged.

Concrete failure modes (backend app/routes/partner_groups.py accept_invite:595 / decline_invite:659):
- Accept 400 INVITE_NOT_PENDING when the invite was already accepted/declined on another device — very reachable because the list is cached (staleTime not forced) and not refetched on failure.
- Accept/Decline 404 GROUP_NOT_FOUND (leader deleted the group) or 404 NOT_INVITED (invite rescinded).
- 500 ACCEPT_FAILED / DECLINE_FAILED on a DB error.
In every case the user taps Accept/Decline and NOTHING visibly happens — no error, no removal, no navigation — so they re-tap indefinitely.

Expected: on failure show an error toast (and refetch [partner-invites] so a stale/consumed invite disappears), matching the exact pattern already fixed elsewhere for the same class — MessagesView (i-20260708-b2f9) and GroupChatView send (i-20260715-30f4) both added onError toasts. PartnerInvites was missed.

Repro: open /partners/invites with an invite that has already been consumed (accept it on a second session first, or have the leader delete the group), tap Accept (or Decline) → observe no feedback and the row remaining.

Fix: add onError to both mutations — toast the error and invalidate/refetch [partner-invites].

issues.description: [bug-hunt] Weekly Review page shows enabled "Approve All Changes" / "Keep Current" buttons on an ALREADY-REVIEWED week, and tapping either always fails with a red "Couldn't save. Try again." toast — with no indication the week was already reviewed. Root cause: WeeklyReviewScreen (src/pages/WeeklyReviewScreen.tsx) renders the actionable <AcceptChangesFlow> whenever a review object exists and NEVER reads review.status. reviewService.getLatest()/getById() (src/services/review.service.ts:115-125) return the review regardless of status, and the backend GET /reviews/latest|current (nyu_backend/app/routes/reviews.py:185-239) returns the current-week (or previous-week) review even when status==="reviewed". But the POST handlers reject any non-pending review: approve_review/modify_review/reject_review (reviews.py:279-280, 320-321, 416-417) each guard with "if review.status not in (pending_review, pending_data): return _err(Review is already {status})" (HTTP 400). AcceptChangesFlow.handleSubmit (src/components/review/AcceptChangesFlow.tsx:43-64) catches that and only shows toast({title:"Couldn't save", description:"Try again."}) — so every tap errors identically and the user is stuck. Repro: (1) open a weekly review and Approve (or Keep Current) once so status flips to "reviewed"; (2) re-enter /weekly-review — tap the weekly-review card in the Notifications inbox (src/pages/Notifications.tsx:438 navigate("/weekly-review") -> getLatest) or re-tap the push (src/capacitor/push.ts:257 /weekly-review?id=); (3) swipe to the "Plan Changes" section — the Approve/Keep Current buttons are enabled with no "already reviewed" state; (4) tap "Approve All Changes" or "Keep Current" -> red "Couldn't save. Try again." toast; retrying fails the same way. Expected: an already-reviewed week should render a read-only / "You've already reviewed this week" state (mirror the existing 'completed' success block) or disable the action buttons — not enabled CTAs that always 400. Fix: gate AcceptChangesFlow behind review.status — when status is not "pending_review"/"pending_data", show the reviewed summary instead of the actionable flow (and/or seed the 'completed'-style branch from review.status on mount).

fix.description: Root cause ran deeper than the UI: after the Saturday 'review ready' push a weekly review sits in the 'notified' state for the whole action window, but the backend AND the screen only allowed Approve/Keep on a 'pending' review -- so tapping the push's Approve CTA always failed with 'Couldn't save', and re-opening any finished week showed the same dead-end buttons. Fix (full-stack): the backend now accepts approve/keep/modify on a notified review and the screen keeps those actions live through the review window (first image), while a genuinely finished week (already reviewed/applied) shows a clean read-only summary instead of buttons that always error (second image).

Now fixed full-stack (backend guard + FE gate + type) and deployed.

heading plus a "7-day avg X.Xh" figure (lines 84-101), then embeds (line 105). But SleepQualityChart (src/components/charts/SleepQualityChart.tsx) is a self-contained standalone widget that ALSO renders its own

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Recipe steps: the FIRST cooking instruction is rendered as an unnumbered bullet '•' labeled (for screen readers) 'Recipe note:' — as if it were a preamble — and every remaining step is numbered off-by-one with the step count one short. A 6-step recipe shows an unnumbered first step, then 'Step 1 of 5' … 'Step 5 of 5'.

Route: /recipe-detail (open any recipe meal from Nutrition → the 'Instructions' section). Also affects the collapsible 'Recipe' block on the meal-detail screen.

Expected: instructions render 'Step 1 of N' … 'Step N of N', the first real step numbered 1. Actual: the first instruction shows a '•' bullet + aria-label 'Recipe note: <first step>', numbering starts at '1' on the SECOND step, and the total is N-1.

Root cause (src/components/RecipeStepList.tsx): the renderer UNCONDITIONALLY treats finalSteps[0] as a preamble — isPreamble = (i === 0) (lines 100 & 132), stepNum = i (so the 2nd element becomes 'Step 1'), and totalSteps = finalSteps.length - 1 (line 90). That is only correct when a leading preamble was actually extracted. But (a) the `steps` prop — used by RecipeDetail as steps={recipe.instructions} — is documented at line 48 as 'Pre-split step strings' with NO preamble, so instructions[0] is a real step; and (b) splitRecipeSteps(notes) only prepends a preamble element when preamble TEXT precedes the first marker — for the common notes that start directly with '1) …' it returns pure steps (see the component's own test, lines 170-174), so notes[0] is also a real step.

Node-verified render decision (replicating lines 90/100/101/108/116):
CASE A steps=['Heat oil…','Add onions…','Add spices…','Serve hot'] -> '[•] Recipe note: Heat oil…' / 'Step 1 of 3: Add onions…' / 'Step 2 of 3' / 'Step 3 of 3' (4 instructions shown as 1 note + 3 numbered).
CASE B notes='1) Boil pasta 2) Make sauce 3) Combine' -> splits to 3 real steps -> first shown as '[•] Recipe note: Boil pasta', then 'Step 1 of 2' / 'Step 2 of 2'.
CASE C notes WITH a genuine preamble ('Prep + cook ~20 min. 1) …') renders correctly — confirming the code only works when a preamble is actually present.

Repro: 1) Open /recipe-detail for any recipe whose instructions start with the first step (i.e. no 'Prep ~X min' preamble). 2) Scroll to Instructions. Expected step 1 is shown as an unnumbered bullet and the visible numbering / 'Step k of M' count is off by one.

Fix: only treat index 0 as a preamble when it genuinely is one (e.g. have splitRecipeSteps return a hasPreamble flag or prepend a sentinel, or detect that element 0 lacks a leading numeric marker). For the `steps` prop path, number from 1 with totalSteps = length. The existing RecipeStepList tests do NOT lock the buggy path — they only seed a preamble at [0] and never assert numbering for the no-preamble / raw-`steps` cases.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Body Measurements: typing a value into the measurement number field does nothing — the field silently reverts to the previously-logged value (or 0.00 if none) on the very next render, so a typed value can never be committed. Only the +/- stepper buttons work.

Repro: 1) Open /measurements. 2) Tap the large number field under "Record New Measurement". 3) Type any number (e.g. 45). Expected: field shows 45. Actual: field immediately snaps back to the seeded value (last-logged value for that body part, or 0.00 for a first-ever measurement).

Verified via Playwright on localhost:8080 with a mocked /measurements/ overview (seeded history=33 for Right Arm): typing "45" left the input at "33"; the + button by contrast updates correctly (33 -> steps).

Root cause: the re-seed effect in src/pages/Measurements.tsx (lines 310-321) re-runs on every render (its dep allTypeHistories is a fresh array each render from useQueries) and calls seedFromLatest() whenever userEdited.current is false, overwriting the input. The +/- buttons set userEdited.current=true (lines 580 & 589) so they are exempt, but the text <input> onChange (lines 560-567) never sets userEdited.current, so every keystroke is wiped. Same class as the prior QA i-20260704-22f4 fix (which guarded the steppers) — the text-input path was missed.

Fix: set userEdited.current=true inside the input onChange when a valid value is entered (mirror the stepper buttons). Impact: a first-ever measurement (0 seed) can otherwise only be reached by tapping + up to ~190 times to hit 95cm.
issues.author: shakeebshaan

fix.description: Typing a value into the Body Measurements field did nothing — it snapped back to the last-logged value (or 0) on the next render, because only the +/- buttons were treated as a user edit. The text field now records typed input as an edit too, so a typed value sticks. Proof: seeded to 33, typed 45, and it stayed 45.

judge.note: Root-cause fix mirrors the stepper's userEdited guard; regression test fails-before/passes-after; live screenshot shows typed 45 persisting over the 33 seed.

judge.note: Header overflow reproduced at 375px (docScrollW 502>375, offender=.chips 429px). Fix: .bar/.chips flex-wrap; re-measured docScrollW=375=vw, no horizontal scroll. Full-viewport 375px capture shows the wrapped 2-row header and board fitting.

fix.description: Root cause: the supplement tracker was localStorage-only (nyus_supplement_data), so it was lost on the native webview after logout, never synced across devices, lived on the Dashboard (not the Diet page), and the coach had no adherence data. Fix: added server persistence (new supplement_data table + GET/PUT /api/v1/supplements, backend d2b9b7a deployed) — the card now reconciles with the server on mount, migrates existing device-local items up once, and PUTs every change (localStorage kept as offline cache). Moved the card from Dashboard into the Nutrition (Diet) page below Fine-tune your plan. Today's adherence now feeds the coach context. Screenshot: the Diet page showing the server-loaded item (proven E2E: PUT then GET returns it across requests).

judge.note: All sub-asks addressed: tracked inside Diet page, server-persisted (survives logout/device switch), fed to coach context, mirrors the activity-tracking pattern. Verified E2E on prod (PUT then GET persists) + full-screen Diet capture; tsc clean, 20/20 supplement tests green, backend deployed.
